purpose: A waitlist signup form for a website: only the email is required, the other questions are optional, and it still posts with no script.
namedChanges: The field rules (lengths, allowed answers, the email shape, the notice stored word for word) are read from `workers/waitlist-fields.ts` at the same commit and written as `src/fields.ts`, with a neutral default field list in different lengths and choice values; the host passes `fields` and its server validates that same list.

Ids are per instance from Vue's `useId`, built as `<id>-field-<name>`, `<id>-help-<name>`, `<id>-error-<name>` and `<id>-option-<name>-<value>`, with every character in a name or value other than a letter or digit written as `_<hex>_` so two names can never give one id; the source used fixed `wl-*` ids.
The source's sentences are not in the unit: labels, help, options, notice, button and thank-you are `fields`, `labels` and `notice`, with neutral English defaults.
The source's dev-build skip of the request (`import.meta.dev`) is not here; pass `send` for a preview.
Tailwind is written out as plain CSS; no utility class and no `@apply`.
The button is disabled while sending; the source left it focusable with `aria-disabled`.
The token wait is `tokenWaitMs`, default 8 seconds; the source waited 15.

An error clears as soon as that field's answer is valid, on every field (on `input` or `change`, that field only). The source did this for the email field only. A new error is never added while typing.

New prop `noScriptAction` (default empty). With no script the form posts to the current page, as the source's `<form method="post">` with no `action` did; with `noScriptAction` set, to that address. `actionUrl` is only where the script sends the JSON. With a Turnstile key set, a post with no script carries no token, so a server that checks Turnstile refuses it.
When the `sent` slot holds no `h1`, `h2`, `h3` or `[tabindex="-1"]` element, focus goes to the sent wrapper itself (`tabindex="-1"`); the source had no slot.
When `fields` changes after mount, a new choice field opens on its `defaultValue`.

The source's phone question and "which AI" question are not in the default list; add a `tel` or `choice` field for them. The source's honeypot is the `honeypot` prop, off by default (the source always drew its `website` trap). The body holds only declared fields, plus `page`, `notice`, `turnstileToken` and the honeypot when set (not when its name clashes with a field or one of those keys).
A choice field's `look` (`tiles` or `pills`) and `columns` (1 or 2) say how its answers are drawn; the source hard-coded tiles for two questions and pills for one.
An invalid field, and every answer of an invalid choice, has the danger border as well as its message; the source showed the message only.

The default thank-you block is a plain heading and line in the page's font (24px/32px weight 600 in `--site-block-success`, then the body); the source used its display face, clamped from 2rem to 2.8rem (44.8px on a wide screen). The `sent` slot replaces the block.
The form's root is capped at `maxWidth` (default `40rem`); the source form had no cap. Pass `max-width="none"` for the source's width.
